scope: Source-certified partial single-column BINARY indexes: actual predicate/unique key rows, CREATE/open/DDL/transactions, accepted-point IGNORE/REPLACE and counters, independent physical key checks and rollback/WAL encoding. Finite admitted SQL/file behavior, not global SQLite equivalence.

negative_results.reason: SQL rejected WHERE indexes and independent opening rejected native SQLite files containing them.
Rollback cases passed apart from four unique cases. The WAL encoder was still called without filtered declarations, causing 27 additional failures.

negative_results.stage: Both image paths plus catalog-ordered roots
negative_results.reason: Both original named partial-index probes pass. Unique partial-index creation/conflict behavior remained explicitly unsupported.
Unique CREATE, active duplicate rejection and inactive duplicates pass, including large overflow/mixed keys. Explicit IGNORE/REPLACE still required native actions.

IGNORE skips actual row/output phases but retains AUTOINCREMENT allocation. REPLACE removes actual victims, freezes registers and accounts auxiliary FK deletes without direct counts. All file cases match.
Abort, skip/replace, update actions, multi-row prefixes, NULLs, predicate errors, sequence effects and FK phase controls match the pinned non-bailing shell.

implementation: CoreCatalogData.FilteredIndex retains independently replayed source and owner identity. The source-aware catalog owns these definitions and transaction snapshots; ordinary Core full-column indexes retain their existing model and proofs.

CorePartialIndex prepares actual columns/predicates against real schemas, selects actual source rows, sorts with the existing BINARY key comparator and checks unique active values. SQL NULL uniqueness and predicate truth remain ordinary scalar semantics.

Pure and IO file opening decode the actual physical index tree and compare every key/rowid to the actual qualifying source rows. Generated-image fast paths remain unchanged; filtered declarations use the independently checked compatibility path. Namespace duplicates are rejected during acquisition.

The existing index-cell, overflow and page-size machinery encodes real qualifying keys. Both rollback and WAL pass actual filtered sources/identities into the encoder; mixed ordinary/filtered index plans follow catalog creation order. The ordinary/filtered basic root identity regression is retained.

Actual accepted candidate checking runs before publication. Typed skip decisions implement IGNORE without message-based control signals and retain sequence allocation. REPLACE freezes actual registers/rowids, removes actual victims, preserves caller counters and accounts FK mutations before the accepted point.

Direct and virtual schema PRAGMAs share state-aware index metadata with actual partial/unique flags. CREATE/open/drop, rollback/savepoints and schema cookie/identity changes retain the certified objects. The C VFS shim is unchanged.

evaluation_protocols.public_file_modes: 7334 complete stdout/exit/first-error and independent persisted catalog/row/integrity comparisons in rollback/WAL file modes, including 88 new partial-index cases with SQLite-origin files, unique actions, overflow/mixed keys and basic root identity.
evaluation_protocols.same_connection: 167 retained continuation API cases plus 29 separately reported partial-index API cases, total 196. Both use the actual state-carrying Core API versus the pinned non-bailing shell with fresh final generated inputs.
evaluation_protocols.select_input_regressions: All 12 independently selectable SELECT regressions remain passing and are separate from API/file totals.
evaluation_protocols.crashes: 372 SIGKILL timing samples, including 24 new retained partial-index entered/left-key samples. Independent SQLite validates recovered rows, catalog SQL, index flags/keys, cookie and integrity. No every-syscall, power-loss, arbitrary-schedule or global root-page-identity claim.
evaluation_protocols.named_features: Original named failures decrease from eight to six in 88 probes: WITHOUT ROWID, composite primary keys and expression indexes, both modes. This finite survey is not a global coverage percentage.

proof_scope: All retained contracts and audits compile. New audited component laws couple filtered definitions to actual source text, preserve selected-row membership and actual predicate truth, and retain single-row unique-check behavior. Existing checked-image decoding and journal recovery contracts now execute the filtered physical-key checks. The maintained executable group covers predicates, metadata, transactions and actual IGNORE/REPLACE states. No global partial-index/planner/SQL equivalence theorem is claimed.
limitations: Six named feature failures remain: WITHOUT ROWID, composite primary keys and expression indexes in both file modes.

Partial index planner selection is not implemented; query execution keeps ordinary checked table/full-index plans. Recursive partial REPLACE with DELETE programs, non-ABORT declared primary policies, ALTER, UPSERT, non-BINARY declarations and broader schema-function/error combinations remain work.
Bulk physical root-page layout is not globally SQLite-identical; pending new-object schema metadata and larger root-preservation cases remain separate work.
Wider error codes/phases, FAIL/IGNORE/ROLLBACK controls, triggered UPSERT, INSTEAD OF/temp triggers, writable CTEs, trigger-aware ALTER and deferred private-function declarations remain work.

UTF-16 writes/setters, native-key/materialization limits, pending new physical allocations and earlier SQL/storage limitations remain. The finite process-kill samples do not establish every syscall/power-loss schedule.
